verses.html: The second lot came out for Simeon, even for the tribe of the children of Simeon according to their families.
They had for their inheritance Beersheba (or Sheba), Moladah,
Hazar Shual, Balah, Ezem,
Eltolad, Bethul, Hormah,
Ziklag, Beth Marcaboth, Hazar Susah,
Beth Lebaoth, and Sharuhen; thirteen cities with their villages;
Ain, Rimmon, Ether, and Ashan; four cities with their villages;
and all the villages that were around these cities to Baalath Beer, Ramah of the South.1
Out of the part of the children of Judah was the inheritance of the children of Simeon; for the portion of the children of Judah was too much for them.<sup class="footnote-marker">2</sup>
The third lot came up for the children of Zebulun according to their families.
Their border went up westward, even to Maralah, and reached to Dabbesheth.
It turned from Sarid eastward toward the sunrise to the border of Chisloth Tabor.
From there it passed along eastward to Gath Hepher, to Ethkazin; and it went out at Rimmon which stretches to Neah.
The border turned around it on the north to Hannathon; and it ended at the valley of Iphtah El;
Kattath, Nahalal, Shimron, Idalah, and Bethlehem3: twelve cities with their villages.
This is the inheritance of the children of Zebulun according to their families, these cities with their villages.
The fourth lot came out for Issachar, even for the children of Issachar according to their families.
Their border was to Jezreel4, Chesulloth, Shunem,
Hapharaim, Shion, Anaharath,
Rabbith, Kishion, Ebez,
Remeth, Engannim, En Haddah, and Beth Pazzez.
The border reached to Tabor, Shahazumah, and Beth Shemesh.
This is the inheritance of the tribe of the children of Issachar according to their families, the cities with their villages.
The fifth lot came out for the tribe of the children of Asher according to their families.
Their border was Helkath, Hali, Beten, Achshaph,
Allammelech, Amad, Mishal. It reached to Carmel westward, and to Shihorlibnath.
It turned toward the sunrise to Beth Dagon, and reached to Zebulun, and to the valley of Iphtah El northward to Beth Emek and Neiel.
and Ebron, Rehob, Hammon, and Kanah, even to great Sidon.
The border turned to Ramah, to the fortified city of Tyre; and the border turned to Hosah.
Ummah also, and Aphek5, and Rehob: twenty-two cities with their villages.
This is the inheritance of the tribe of the children of Asher according to their families, these cities with their villages.
The sixth lot came out for the children of Naphtali, even for the children of Naphtali according to their families.
Their border was from Heleph, from the oak in Zaanannim, Adami-nekeb, and Jabneel, to Lakkum.
The border turned westward to Aznoth Tabor, and went out from there to Hukkok.
The fortified cities were Ziddim, Zer, Hammath, Rakkath, Chinnereth,
Adamah, Ramah, Hazor,
Kedesh, Edrei6, En Hazor,
Iron, Migdal El, Horem, Beth Anath, and Beth Shemesh; nineteen cities with their villages.
This is the inheritance of the tribe of the children of Naphtali according to their families, the cities with their villages.
The seventh lot came out for the tribe of the children of Dan according to their families.
The border of their inheritance was Zorah, Eshtaol, Irshemesh,
Shaalabbin, Aijalon, Ithlah,
Elon, Timnah, Ekron,
Eltekeh, Gibbethon, Baalath,
Jehud, Bene Berak, Gath Rimmon,
Me Jarkon, and Rakkon, with the border opposite Joppa.
The border of the children of Dan went up and fought against Leshem, took it, struck it with the edge of the sword, and possessed it, and called Leshem, Dan.7
This is the inheritance of the tribe of the children of Dan according to their families, these cities with their villages.
So they finished distributing the land for inheritance by its borders.
According to Yahweh’s commandment, they gave him the city which he asked, even Timnathserah8 in the hill country of Ephraim; and he built the city, and lived there.

These are the inheritances, which Eleazar the priest, Joshua the son of Nun, and the heads of the fathers’ houses of the tribes of the children of Israel, distributed for inheritance by lot in Shiloh.

footnotes.html: Baalath Beer / Ramah of the South (v. 8) — generally treated as a single double-named site (‘Baalath of the well, Ramah of the Negev’), the same place David sent spoil to in 1 Sam 30:27 ('Ramoth-negev'). The location is unknown.

Simeon embedded in Judah (v. 9) — the Simeonite city list overlaps almost completely with Judah’s Negev district of 15:21-32, which is what the verse acknowledges: Simeon receives no separate territory but cities carved out of the larger Judahite portion. Simeon’s polygon on this map is therefore a notional Negev block; in practice the tribe shares Judah’s southern allotment, and is absorbed by it before the monarchy.
Bethlehem of Zebulun (v. 15) is the village northwest of Nazareth, distinct from the Judahite Bethlehem of Ruth, David, and the gospels. The judge Ibzan is buried here (Judg 12:8-10).
Jezreel (v. 18) — the Issacharite Jezreel at Tel Yizreel, royal residence of Ahab and Jezebel (1 Kgs 21). Distinct from the Judahite Jezreel of 15:56.

Aphek (v. 30) is now a fourth distinct Aphek in this edition: the Asherite Aphek at Tel Afek (Tell Kurdaneh) east of Acco, alongside the Sharon Aphek (12:18), the Aphek of the Amorites (13:4), and the hill-country Aphekah (15:53).
Edrei (v. 37) here is a Naphtalite town distinct from the great Bashan Edrei of 12:4 / 13:12 (Daraa, Syria). The Naphtali Edrei has not been securely located.

Leshem renamed Dan (v. 47) — the Danite migration narrative of Judges 18 (where the city is called Laish) tells the same story at much greater length and gives the conquest a different motivation: a partial failure to hold the southern allotment forced the tribe northward. Tel Dan (Tell el-Qadi) at the foot of Mount Hermon, where the principal source of the Jordan rises, became the northern anchor of Israelite territory ('from Dan to Beersheba').

Timnath-Serah (v. 50) — Joshua’s personal allotment, generally located at Khirbet Tibneh c. 25 km north of Jerusalem in the hill country of Ephraim. The variant Timnath-Heres in Judg 2:9 is generally regarded as a metathesis of the same name; it is also the site of his burial in Josh 24:30.
